title: Seepage vs. Reservoir Level Relationship (Normal Behavior)

n.description: Exponent (typically 1.0–2.0; n=1 for Darcy flow, n>1 for increasing gradient)

applicability: Establish baseline relationship during normal operations. Plot Q vs. (H_res - H_tw). Departures from the established trend indicate changed seepage conditions — investigate immediately. Turbid seepage or seepage carrying fines is always critical regardless of quantity.

title: HST Model — Concrete Dam Displacement
equation: δ = Σ(aᵢ × Hⁱ) + Σ(bⱼ × sin(2πjt/365) + cⱼ × cos(2πjt/365)) + d₁×θ + d₂×θ²

H.description: Reservoir level (polynomial terms for hydrostatic effect)

t.description: Day of year (harmonic terms for seasonal/thermal effect)

θ.description: Time since reference date (linear + quadratic for irreversible trends)

aᵢ, bⱼ, cⱼ, d₁, d₂.description: Regression coefficients fitted to historical data

applicability: Standard statistical model for concrete dam behavior. Fit to 5–10+ years of historical data. Prediction residuals (measured - modeled) flagged when exceeding ±2–3 standard deviations. Used worldwide (EDF, USBR, USACE).

title: Uplift Pressure — Measured vs. Design
equation: U_measured = γ_w × h_piezometer;  Safety check: U_measured ≤ U_design

U_measured.description: Measured uplift pressure at foundation piezometer

U_design.description: Design uplift assumption (e.g., USBR: P_drain = Pd + 1/3(Pu-Pd) with functional drains)

applicability: Compare measured uplift to design assumptions at each piezometer location. If measured exceeds design, stability analysis must be revised. Drain effectiveness = 1 - (P_measured - P_downstream)/(P_upstream - P_downstream).

title: Settlement Rate Assessment
equation: ṡ = Δs/Δt;  Alert if ṡ > ṡ_threshold

ṡ.description: Rate of settlement (crest or embankment surface)

ṡ_threshold.description: Site-specific threshold rate (typically alarm if > 10–25 mm/yr for mature embankment dams)

applicability: During first filling and early life, settlement is expected and may be rapid. After initial consolidation (3–5 years), settlement rate should decrease logarithmically. Accelerating settlement or differential settlement is always an alert condition.

title: Critical Hydraulic Gradient (Internal Erosion Screening)

i_cr.description: Critical hydraulic gradient for heave/piping initiation

applicability: Typical i_cr ≈ 1.0 for most soils. Measured exit gradient (from piezometer data) should be well below i_cr. Safety factor: FS = i_cr / i_exit ≥ 3–5 (USACE). This is a simplified check — actual internal erosion involves multiple mechanisms beyond simple heave.

title: Drain Effectiveness

E_drain.description: Drain effectiveness (0 = no effect, 1 = fully effective)

P_m.description: Measured piezometric pressure at drain line

applicability: USBR assumes 2/3 drain effectiveness (E = 0.67) for design. USACE assumes E = 0.50 for design. Measured E should be tracked over time — declining effectiveness indicates drain clogging and requires remedial action. If E drops below design assumption, stability must be re-evaluated.
